pk.context: 60 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: A boxed warning on reduced efficacy above 95 mL/min creatinine clearance sets this factor Xa inhibitor apart.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is 62%, and food does not affect total exposure. About 55% is bound to plasma proteins in vitro, and roughly half of clearance is renal.
A tosylate monohydrate salt; the active moiety has a molecular weight of 548.1. It is slightly soluble in water at pH 3 to 5 and practically insoluble at pH 8 to 9.
Approved under an NDA as 15, 30 and 60 mg tablets, dosed once daily.

Boxed warnings for reduced efficacy above 95 mL/min creatinine clearance, early discontinuation, and spinal or epidural hematoma. Contraindicated with active bleeding; bleeding and anemia are most common.
Reducing stroke and systemic embolism in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, and treating deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism after 5 to 10 days of parenteral anticoagulant.
A selective factor Xa inhibitor that needs no antithrombin III, blocking free factor Xa and thrombin-induced platelet aggregation.
The generic name begins with E and has eight letters.
